concept.name: Change Data Capture (CDC)

relationships.description: Connects Change Data Capture (CDC) to database indexing in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Change Data Capture (CDC) streams row-level inserts, updates, and deletes directly from a database's transaction log (WAL/binlog/oplog) into event buses like Kafka—eliminating dual-write race conditions and heavy polling queries.
spark.keyTakeaway: Stop dual-writing to your database and Kafka in application code: tail the committed transaction log (e.g., Debezium + PostgreSQL `pgoutput`) and pair it with the Transactional Outbox pattern for schema-safe, at-least-once event streaming.

concept.whyItMatters: Modern architectures constantly need to sync an OLTP database with search indices (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch), caches (Redis), analytics warehouses (Snowflake/BigQuery), and downstream microservices. Application-level dual writes (`db.save()` followed by `kafka.send()`) inevitably diverge when a process crashes or times out between the two calls, while `SELECT * WHERE updated_at > ?` polling misses hard deletes, burdens primary replicas, and adds seconds to minutes of lag. Log-based CDC turns the database's own durability log into an ordered, zero-polling event stream.
whenToUse: Synchronizing OLTP state (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle) to read replicas, Elasticsearch, Redis, or data lakes in near real-time (<500 ms lag) without impacting transactional latency.
Implementing the Transactional Outbox pattern so domain events are atomically committed in the same ACID transaction as business state.
Zero-downtime database migrations (e.g., MySQL 5.7 to Aurora 8.0 or monolith-to-microservice table extraction) via continuous replication and shadow verification.
whenNotToUse: When simple batch ETL (hourly or nightly `COPY` / `pg_dump`) satisfies analytics SLAs and running Kafka Connect + Debezium adds unjustified operational overhead.
When downstream consumers need rich domain context that spans 5 joined tables and isn't materialized in a single row—unless paired with an Outbox table containing the domain payload.
On managed databases where transaction log access (`wal_level=logical` or `binlog_format=ROW`) is disabled or restricted by vendor tier.
keyPoints: Log-based CDC (Debezium, Maxwell, Airbyte CDC) reads the append-only WAL/binlog sequentially, adding negligible I/O overhead compared to trigger-based CDC or `SELECT` polling.
CDC guarantees **at-least-once** delivery and **per-key ordering** (when partitioned by primary key in Kafka); downstream consumers must still be idempotent using LSN/offset or `version` checks.
Initial snapshots (consistent `REPEATABLE READ` table reads + seamless switchover to the WAL LSN) allow bootstrapping terabyte-scale tables without taking downtime.
Schema evolution is a first-class concern: pairing CDC with a Schema Registry (Avro/Protobuf) prevents an `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` from silently breaking downstream Flink or ClickHouse sinks.
Unbounded replication slots (e.g., an abandoned PostgreSQL logical replication slot) will retain WAL segments indefinitely until the primary database disk fills up and crashes.

examples.title: PostgreSQL + Debezium Outbox for E-Commerce Order Events
examples.scenario: An order service previously wrote to PostgreSQL and published to Kafka in Java code. During network blips, 0.3% of paid orders never reached the fulfillment Kafka topic, causing silent shipping failures.
examples.outcome: The team introduced an `outbox_events` table written inside the same `@Transactional` block as `orders`, with Debezium tailing `pgoutput` and transforming payloads via Kafka Connect's `EventRouter` SMT. Dual-write drift dropped to 0%, and `outbox_events` rows are deleted immediately after insert (still captured in WAL) to keep table size near zero.

examples.title: Real-Time Catalog Search Sync to OpenSearch
examples.scenario: A marketplace with 40M SKUs polled MySQL every 60 seconds using `updated_at`, missing `DELETE` operations and spiking primary CPU to 85% during bulk seller price updates.
examples.outcome: Deploying Debezium MySQL (`binlog_format=ROW`) -> Kafka -> OpenSearch Sink cut catalog-to-search propagation lag from 60 seconds to 350 ms, captured hard deletes via Kafka tombstones, and reduced primary MySQL read load by 35%.

tradeOffs.factor: Raw Table CDC vs. Transactional Outbox Pattern
tradeOffs.pro: Raw table CDC requires zero application code changes and captures every column mutation automatically.
tradeOffs.con: Exposes internal database schemas as public contracts—any column rename breaks consumers—whereas the Outbox pattern decouples internal schema from stable versioned domain events.

tradeOffs.pro: Log-based CDC reads sequential WAL files asynchronously with ~1–3% CPU overhead and zero impact on write transaction latency.
tradeOffs.con: Trigger-based CDC writes shadow tables inside the user transaction (adding 2x write amplification and lock contention), though it works on legacy DBs without WAL access.

tradeOffs.factor: Incremental Snapshotting vs. Blocking Initial Snapshot
tradeOffs.pro: Debezium incremental snapshots (DBLog algorithm) chunk large tables with watermarks, allowing pause/resume and avoiding long-held locks or replication slot bloat.
tradeOffs.con: Takes longer to complete the initial backfill than a single parallelized bulk export and requires a primary key on the source table.

failureModes.name: WAL / Binlog Disk Exhaustion
failureModes.description: If the Debezium connector crashes or stalls for hours, PostgreSQL retains all unacknowledged WAL segments in `pg_wal` until the primary disk hits 100% and halts all writes.
failureModes.mitigation: Set `max_slot_wal_keep_size` in PostgreSQL 13+, monitor `pg_replication_slots` lag in bytes, and configure PagerDuty alerts at 50% WAL retention threshold.

failureModes.name: Schema Change Deserialization Crash
failureModes.description: A developer runs `ALTER TABLE` (e.g., changing column type or dropping a non-null field), causing downstream Kafka consumers or BigQuery sinks to fail deserialization and stall the entire partition.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce Schema Registry `BACKWARD` compatibility, test DDL changes in staging with Debezium running, and prefer additive nullable columns.

failureModes.name: Duplicate Events on Connector Rebalance
failureModes.description: A Kafka Connect worker restarts before committing the latest LSN offset to `__connect_offsets`, replaying the last 500–5,000 WAL events upon recovery.
failureModes.mitigation: Make all downstream sinks idempotent using `UPSERT` keyed on primary key + source LSN/timestamp (`source.lsn` or `ts_ms`) so older replays never overwrite newer state.

failureModes.name: Heartbeat Starvation on Low-Traffic Databases
failureModes.description: On a quiet database with active replication slots on a busy shared cluster, Debezium's confirmed LSN never advances because the tracked table has no writes, pinning WAL files from other busy databases.
failureModes.mitigation: Configure `heartbeat.interval.ms=10000` and `heartbeat.action.query` writing to a lightweight heartbeat table so the replication slot LSN advances continuously.

commonMistakes: Exposing raw internal table schemas directly to 10+ downstream microservices, turning every database normalization refactor into a cross-team breaking change.
Forgetting to set `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` in PostgreSQL when downstream consumers need the `before` image of `UPDATE` and `DELETE` rows (default only logs primary keys).
Running `SELECT *` initial snapshots on multi-terabyte tables without incremental chunking, exhausting `tempdb`/undo logs or timing out the replication slot.
Assuming CDC delivers events exactly once—skipping idempotency checks in consumers and corrupting aggregates during Kafka Connect rebalances.
Ignoring TOASTed columns in PostgreSQL (`unchanged-toast-placeholder`), causing `UPDATE` events on unrelated columns to emit placeholder values instead of full text/JSONB blobs.

sections.content:
## The idea

Change Data Capture (CDC) converts a database's internal **write-ahead log (WAL)** or **binary log (binlog)** into an append-only stream of committed row-level mutations (`INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`).

Every ACID database already writes every committed change sequentially to its transaction log for crash recovery and physical replication. Log-based CDC attaches a lightweight reader (such as **Debezium** via PostgreSQL's `pgoutput` logical decoding plugin or MySQL's row-based binlog) to that log. Because it only emits changes *after* `COMMIT` and reads sequentially in the background, it eliminates dual-write inconsistency without adding locks or polling queries to the hot OLTP path.

## Concrete walkthrough

Follow a single order update through a **PostgreSQL -> Debezium -> Kafka -> OpenSearch** pipeline:

1. **ACID Commit:** The Order Service updates `orders SET status = 'SHIPPED' WHERE id = 9041` and (optionally) inserts a row into `outbox_events` within one transaction. PostgreSQL appends the change to `pg_wal` at LSN `0/1A4F890`.
2. **Logical Decoding:** PostgreSQL's `pgoutput` slot decodes the WAL record (including `before` and `after` images if `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` is set) and streams it over the replication protocol to the Debezium Kafka Connect worker.
3. **Envelope & Schema Serialization:** Debezium wraps the mutation in a structured envelope (`op: "u"`, `before`, `after`, `source.lsn`, `ts_ms`), validates it against Confluent Schema Registry (Avro/Protobuf), and produces it to Kafka topic `db.public.orders` partitioned by `key = 9041`.
4. **Offset Commit:** Periodically, Kafka Connect commits `lsn: 0/1A4F890` to its internal `__connect_offsets` topic and sends a standby status feedback to PostgreSQL, allowing old WAL segments to be recycled.
5. **Idempotent Sink:** The OpenSearch sink reads the event, checks `source.lsn` (or version), and executes an idempotent `_update` on document `9041`—achieving <300 ms end-to-end search freshness.

sections.content:
## The Transactional Outbox pattern

Exposing raw database tables via CDC couples downstream consumers to your internal schema. The **Transactional Outbox** pattern solves this cleanly:

1. Instead of streaming `orders` and `order_items` directly, your service inserts a serialized domain event (`OrderConfirmedV2`) into an `outbox` table (`id`, `aggregatetype`, `aggregateid`, `payload`, `created_at`) inside the **exact same ACID transaction** as the business update.
2. Immediately after the insert (or via a background sweep), the row can even be deleted—because PostgreSQL still records the `INSERT` in the WAL, keeping the live `outbox` table tiny.
3. Debezium's `EventRouter` Single Message Transform (SMT) reads only `op = 'c'` (create) events from `outbox`, routes them to `outbox.event.<aggregatetype>` keyed by `aggregateid`, and strips the raw Debezium envelope so consumers receive clean, versioned domain events.

## CDC approaches compared

| Approach | Overhead on Primary DB | Captures Hard Deletes | Latency | Operational Complexity |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Log-Based CDC** (Debezium, Maxwell) | Very Low (~1–3% CPU, sequential log read) | Yes (WAL/binlog `DELETE` + tombstones) | 100–500 ms | Medium–High (Kafka Connect, slot monitoring) |
| **Transactional Outbox + CDC** | Very Low (1 extra small `INSERT` per tx) | N/A (explicit domain events) | 100–500 ms | Medium (requires Outbox table + SMT config) |
| **Trigger-Based CDC** | High (2x write amplification + lock contention) | Yes (via `AFTER DELETE` trigger) | 100 ms – 5 s | Low–Medium (lives inside DB, no WAL access needed) |
| **Timestamp Polling** (`WHERE updated_at > ?`) | High (repeated index/table scans) | No (requires soft-delete flags) | 5 s – 15 min | Low (simple cron or Airbyte/JDBC connector) |

## Failure modes

- **Unbounded Replication Slot Bloat:** A stopped Debezium connector holds back PostgreSQL's `restart_lsn`, filling `pg_wal` until the database crashes with `No space left on device`.
- **Split-Brain Ordering Across Tables:** Partitioning `orders` and `order_items` into different Kafka topics means a consumer can receive `OrderItemCreated` before `OrderCreated`; use the Outbox pattern to bundle aggregates or buffer out-of-order children.
- **Snapshot Timeout / Lock Contention:** Running a legacy blocking snapshot on a busy 2 TB table triggers long-running transaction bloat (`xmin` horizon pinned, blocking `VACUUM`). Always use Debezium's incremental snapshot mode.
- **Silent Data Loss on `max_slot_wal_keep_size`:** If you cap WAL retention to protect disk space and the connector falls behind that cap, PostgreSQL invalidates the slot—requiring an automated alert and incremental re-snapshot.

## Production operations & schema governance

Operating CDC reliably at scale requires treating the pipeline as Tier-1 infrastructure:

- **Schema Registry Enforcement:** Register all Debezium topics in Confluent Schema Registry or Apicurio with `BACKWARD` compatibility. Never run destructive `DROP COLUMN` or type-narrowing DDL without a expand-and-contract migration.
- **Heartbeat & LSN Monitoring:** Alert on `pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), confirmed_flush_lsn)` exceeding 1 GB and enable `heartbeat.interval.ms` on low-write databases.
- **Dead-Letter Queues (DLQ):** Configure `errors.tolerance=all` and `errors.deadletterqueue.topic.name` on sink connectors so one malformed UTF-8 string does not halt replication for millions of valid rows.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Enable `wal_level = logical` (PostgreSQL) or `binlog_format = ROW` + `binlog_row_image = FULL` (MySQL) on the source database.
- [ ] Set `max_slot_wal_keep_size` and alert when replication slot lag exceeds 50% of the cap to prevent primary disk exhaustion.
- [ ] Use the Transactional Outbox pattern for cross-service domain events; reserve raw-table CDC for search, cache, and analytics sinks.
- [ ] Configure `heartbeat.interval.ms` and Debezium incremental snapshots (`signal.data.collection`) for zero-downtime backfills.
- [ ] Enforce idempotent upserts keyed by primary key + `source.lsn` (or `ts_ms`) on every downstream consumer.

interviewProblems.title: Change Data Capture (CDC)
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Change Data Capture (CDC). What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Change Data Capture (CDC) streams row-level inserts, updates, and deletes directly from a database's transaction log (WAL/binlog/oplog) into event buses like Kafka—eliminating dual-write race conditions and heavy polling queries.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Kafka + Schema Registry applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Idempotent Sinks.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Idempotent Sinks experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Set `max_slot_wal_keep_size` in PostgreSQL 13+, monitor `pg_replication_slots` lag in bytes, and configure PagerDuty alerts at 50% WAL retention threshold.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Stop dual-writing to your database and Kafka in application code: tail the committed transaction log (e.g., Debezium + PostgreSQL `pgoutput`) and pair it with the Transactional Outbox pattern for schema-safe, at-least-once event streaming.
Avoid trap: Exposing raw internal table schemas directly to 10+ downstream microservices, turning every database normalization refactor into a cross-team breaking change.
Avoid trap: Forgetting to set `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` in PostgreSQL when downstream consumers need the `before` image of `UPDATE` and `DELETE` rows (default only logs primary keys).

When to reach for it: Synchronizing OLTP state (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle) to read replicas, Elasticsearch, Redis, or data lakes in near real-time (<500 ms lag) without impacting transactional latency.
When to reach for it: Implementing the Transactional Outbox pattern so domain events are atomically committed in the same ACID transaction as business state.

putItTogether.title: Putting Change Data Capture Together
putItTogether.summary: Stop dual-writing to your database and Kafka in application code: tail the committed transaction log (e.g., Debezium + PostgreSQL `pgoutput`) and pair it with the Transactional Outbox pattern for schema-safe, at-least-once event streaming.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Change Data Capture before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: The team introduced an `outbox_events` table written inside the same `@Transactional` block as `orders`, with Debezium tailing `pgoutput` and transforming payloads via Kafka Connect's `EventRouter` SMT. Dual-write drift dropped to 0%, and `outbox_events` rows are deleted immediately after insert (still captured in WAL) to keep table size near zero.
